question: How are GET Route Handlers cached by default in modern Next.js (15+)?
options: They are statically prerendered at build time unless dynamic = 'force-dynamic' is exported.
They are uncached by default and run dynamically on every request unless you explicitly opt into caching.
They are cached in the browser's localStorage for 60 seconds.
They are only cached when the request includes an Authorization header.
explanation: In Next.js 15+, GET Route Handlers are uncached by default so API routes, health checks, and webhook endpoints always run dynamically unless explicitly opted into static caching.

question: Why should a webhook Route Handler read the body with await request.text() before parsing JSON?
options: Because request.json() is deprecated in the Web Fetch specification.
Because cryptographic webhook signatures are computed over the exact raw request body bytes, and re-stringifying parsed JSON can alter whitespace or key order.
Because request.text() automatically validates the x-webhook-signature header.
Because JSON payloads larger than 1 KB cannot be parsed with request.json().
explanation: Webhook providers sign the exact raw byte payload sent over HTTP. Reading await request.text() lets you verify the signature against the exact string before calling JSON.parse().

question: What happens if a webhook Route Handler calls revalidateTag() before verifying the x-webhook-signature header?
options: Next.js automatically rolls back the cache invalidation if the handler later returns 401.
Unauthenticated callers can forge requests to purge your cache repeatedly, causing origin database overload and denial-of-wallet attacks.
revalidateTag() throws a runtime error when called before request.headers.get().
The webhook signature header is automatically deleted by next/cache.
explanation: Cache invalidation takes effect immediately when revalidateTag() is invoked. Always authenticate the webhook signature and validate the payload before invalidating any cache tags.

question: Why is after() well-suited for writing webhook audit logs in a Route Handler after calling revalidateTag(tag, 'max')?
options: Because after() encrypts the audit log payload before writing it.
Because it lets the Route Handler return a fast 202 response to the webhook provider while the audit log write completes in the background.
Because revalidateTag() only takes effect if an after() callback is registered in the same request.
Because after() converts a POST Route Handler into a static route.
explanation: Webhook senders enforce tight response timeouts. Offloading non-critical audit trail persistence to after() keeps the HTTP response fast while ensuring the runtime waits for the log write via waitUntil().
